episodes.160370: Scattered thunderstorms produced several instances of localized wind damage.
episodes.160376: An outflow boundary from overnight storms initiated a round of strong to severe thunderstorms north of Indianapolis before spreading through much of central and south central Indiana. Radar showed numerous weak microburst/downbursts at times through the late morning and early afternoon with minor tree damage noted in Hendricks and Marion county.  Across that same area and also across southern Putnam and northeastern Owen, storms remained stationary which led to pockets of 2-3 inches and flooding.
episodes.160425: Scattered thunderstorms moved through the region during the afternoon hours in association with an upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.160426: Scattered thunderstorms moved through the region during the afternoon hours in association with an upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.160530: Ample low-level moisture and strong daytime heating combined with a weak mid-level wave drifting into the state from the western Atlantic to produce isolated severe thunderstorms across north Georgia.
episodes.160710: Afternoon storms produce strong wind gusts downing power lines and producing minor damage in Pinellas and Lee counties.
episodes.160711: Afternoon storms produce strong marine wind gusts over Tampa Bay and Pinellas and Charlotte waters.
episodes.160736: Several trees around the Knoxville area were blown down by thunderstorm winds. There were a couple of reports of high water on roads.
episodes.160747: An upper level disturbance moved into the Ohio Valley on August 25th, accompanied by a line of showers and thunderstorms that afternoon and evening. This line produced a severe storm in McDowell County which resulted in a few trees to be blown down. Heavy downpours were also observed with this passing disturbance, which resulted in high water that damaged and washed out a few residential bridges.
episodes.160748: An upper level disturbance moved into the Ohio Valley on August 25th, with plenty of daytime heating in place preceding its arrival. This led to the development of a line of showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon in Ohio. One storm in particular resulted in hail in Lawrence County.
episodes.161079: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening of August 24th.
episodes.161080: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and evening of August 24th.
episodes.161081: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois on August 25th producing heavy rain and localized flooding.
episodes.161639: A few severe thunderstorms developed during the mid afternoon hours of August 25.  A landspout was witnessed by law enforcement briefly touching down in a field southwest of Geneseo, IL around 3:40 PM CDT.  Further to the south, a severe thunderstorm produced large hail and damaging winds. Hail at least golf ball sized was reported and severe wind gusts around 60 MPH resulted in damage to tree limbs, power lines, and shingles. Another separate short lived tornado occurred in Warren County, just east of the town of Berwick, IL.
episodes.161640: Heavy rain fell the morning of  August 25th, resulting in some flash flooding in Iowa County. Several inches of rain fell in a few hours.
episodes.161717: A lingering mesoscale convective vortex over northwest Ohio that is acting as a trigger for developing thunderstorms on its eastern flank. 850-300mb mean steering flow, suggested at storm motion had the potential to slow down and create flash flooding in regions downstream (i.e. western PA).
episodes.162101: On August 25th, an outflow boundary produced from afternoon convection in southwestern Kansas moved northward. Thunderstorms developed along this boundary in northwestern Kansas during the evening hours. These thunderstorms yielded hail up to golf balls in size and wind gusts up to 75 mph.  The winds from the thunderstorm also produced a localized dust storm in eastern Greeley county.
episodes.162192: An outflow boundary generated from convection earlier in the day triggered a line of strong to severe thunderstorms from southern Lake Michigan southwestward across north-central Illinois during the late afternoon and evening of August 24th.  As the line dropped southeastward, wind gusts of around 60 mph were observed...causing scattered damage across portions of Fulton, Tazewell, and Champaign counties.
episodes.162193: Isolated supercell thunderstorms developed along old outflow boundaries during the late afternoon and early evening of August 25th.  One cell produced 1-inch diameter hail across portions of Edgar County in east-central Illinois, while another cluster of storms dropped 1-inch diameter hail and caused minor wind damage in Peoria.
episodes.162331: Thunderstorms moving through in the evening hours produced sporadic wind damage, mainly north of M-59.
episodes.162339: Thunderstorm moving through Lake St. Clair produced wind gusts in excess of 40 knots.
episodes.162408: A line of strong storms moved westward off the Florida big bend coast and into Apalachee Bay.  Strong winds gusts in excess of 34 knots were measured along coastal areas.
episodes.162490: A well-defined upper level disturbance moved west from the Bahamas to across South Florida on August 25th and 26th, helping to trigger several periods of strong thunderstorms over the Atlantic waters which spread west over the local waters, then over South Florida and the Gulf of Mexico waters at several times during this period.
episodes.162492: Scattered thunderstorms produced a few localized instances of flooding.
episodes.162498: A well-defined upper level disturbance moved west from the Bahamas to across South Florida on August 25th and 26th, helping to trigger several periods of strong thunderstorms over the Atlantic waters which spread west over the local waters, then over South Florida and the Gulf of Mexico waters at several times during this period.
episodes.162510: An easterly wave moving westward along the south side of an upper ridge encountered some mid level dry air over Central Alabama. The lift associated with the easterly wave and drier mid level air produced favorable conditions for downbursts.
episodes.162514: Surface high pressure was solidly over central Kentucky, but given the moist atmosphere and temperatures in the 90s, afternoon and evening thunderstorms resulted in a variety of severe thunderstorm damage across central Kentucky. Reports ranged from flash flooding and wind damage to a couple of lightning fires.
episodes.162560: Scattered strong storms occurred across the coastal water with multiple reports of a waterspout off the panhandle coast along with gusty winds offshore and along the big bend coast.
episodes.162571: Preexisting outflow boundaries from previous storms and a weak and slow moving cold front al boundary provided opportunities for storms to develop in the early morning hours on the 25th. Overall, the environment was not supportive for organized convection with limited effective bulk shear and elevated nature, but was able to produce a lone thunderstorm wind damage report (trees down). Additionally, precipitable water values in excess of 1.8 inches and slow moving and/or training nature of storms allowed areas to receive heavy rainfall.
episodes.162591: A broken line of storms progressed across south central Lake Michigan and into southwest Michigan and north-central Indiana. Severe winds were reported with some damage. There was also heavy rain with minor flooding.
episodes.162592: A broken line of storms progressed across south central Lake Michigan and into southwest Michigan and north-central Indiana. Severe winds were reported with some damage. There was also heavy rain with minor flooding.
episodes.162692: A small mesoscale convective cluster of storms developed in an area of steep mid-level lapse rates and marginal deep-layer shear. The northern edge of the cluster brushed into far southern South Dakota, with an isolated incident of large hail near the Missouri River.
episodes.162693: Scattered thunderstorms developed over Upstate South Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. A couple of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in the foothills.
episodes.162696: Scattered thunderstorms developed over western North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Lincoln County.
episodes.162740: Isolated thunderstorms across western and northern counties along a stalled surface boundary extended from the leeside trough out of eastern Colorado. Shear and lapse rates were on the low side, but ample instability with DCAPE values around the 1000 J/kg mark allowed for some strong outflow winds to cause damage around the Ingalls area. Otherwise, the remainder of the storms remained below severe thresholds.
episodes.162744: A cold front helped initiate severe weather across eastern Nebraska leading to wind damage and hail.
episodes.162751: A cold front helped initiate severe weather across southwest Iowa leading to wind damage.
episodes.162755: Numerous gale-force wind gusts were recorded in association with showers and thunderstorms as a tropical wave moved slowly west through the Florida Keys.  The tropical wave became amplified due to a middle-to-upper level trough of low pressure progressing westward in advance.
episodes.162756: A long lasting thunderstorm storm in Know and Cedar counties produced strong winds and led to tree damage.
episodes.163038: A broken line of thunderstorms moved into southeastern Lake Michigan, producing strong winds.
episodes.166146: A broad ridge of high pressure was present over the eastern CONUS, with a warm, humid airmass in place over northern OH. PWAT values were near 1.9 and MLCAPE values ranged from 1000-2000 j/kg. Steering flow was minimal, which allowed for slow moving thunderstorms. A single thunderstorm developed over Warren and remained stationary for nearly an hour, before an upstream thunderstorm over Portage County moved east across the Warren area. Radar estimated 2 to 3 of rainfall over northeast Warren over a 2 to 3 hour period, which led to excessive runoff and flash flooding.
